scenes.title: What is dbt & ELT Transformation?
scenes.narration: In this lesson we introduce dbt and the ELT pattern that made it the standard tool for transforming data inside the modern warehouse.

scenes.title: ETL versus ELT

left.heading: ETL
points: Transform on a separate engine before loading

right.heading: ELT
points: Load raw data first, transform in place
Cheap storage and elastic SQL power

scenes.narration: The traditional pattern is ETL, where data is transformed on a separate engine and only the finished result is loaded into the warehouse. dbt embraces ELT instead, loading raw data first and running every transformation as SQL directly inside a powerful cloud warehouse. This shift works because modern warehouses offer cheap storage and elastic compute that make in-warehouse transformation both fast and economical.

scenes.title: What dbt actually is
bullets: A transformation framework, not an ingestion tool
You write SELECT statements; dbt handles the DDL
It layers software engineering onto analytics SQL
scenes.narration: dbt is a transformation framework, so it is deliberately not responsible for extracting or loading data. You simply write a SELECT statement that describes the table you want, and dbt wraps it in the create-or-replace logic needed to build it. In doing so it brings software engineering practices such as version control, testing, and modularity to analytics SQL.

scenes.title: Where dbt sits in the stack
scenes.narration: Picture the pipeline as three stages. An ingestion tool lands raw source data in the warehouse, dbt then transforms that raw data into clean, tested models, and finally business intelligence tools read from the polished marts dbt produces. dbt owns only the middle stage, but that is where most of the analytical logic lives.

scenes.text: dbt turns analytics SQL into reliable, version-controlled software: you describe tables with SELECT statements and dbt builds, tests, and documents them inside your warehouse.
scenes.narration: The core idea to remember is that dbt turns everyday analytics SQL into reliable, version-controlled software, letting you describe tables with SELECT statements while it handles building, testing, and documenting them inside your warehouse.
